query: homeostatic normalization of a dopamine-gated encoding-gain map so low-salience facts are not driven below the recall floor while high-salience facts keep read-stress robustness
source: Turrigiano 2008, 'The Self-Tuning Neuron: Synaptic Scaling of Excitatory Synapses', Cell 135(3):422-435 — homeostatic synaptic scaling MULTIPLICATIVELY scales all of a neuron's synapses to a firing-rate SET POINT while PRESERVING relative synaptic strengths (temporal-correlation info preserved). This is the companion process our static DA-gain clamp replaced: a set-point normalizing the write-gain map to the running DA distribution (mean gain->1.0) removes the low-sigma regression (low-DA facts no longer pushed below the recall floor) WITHOUT giving up high-sigma salience robustness (relative strengths, hence salience ordering, preserved). Cross-ref Turrigiano & Nelson 2004 Nat Rev Neurosci 5:97-107; Turrigiano 2012 CSH Perspect Biol a005736.
